title: Stacks, queues & trees
examples: What is the difference between a stack and a queue?
Can you show me how to traverse a binary tree?
When would I use a stack instead of a queue?

explain.say: Today we look at three important data structures.
A stack follows the Last In First Out rule.
To add an item we use the push operation.
Removing an item is done using the pop operation.
A queue follows the First In First Out rule.
We add items to the rear using enqueue.

faq.q: What does LIFO mean in data structures?
faq.a: LIFO stands for Last In First Out. This means the last item added to the structure is the first one to be removed. It is like a stack of plates.
asks: What is the principle of a stack?

faq.q: When is a queue better than a stack?
faq.a: A queue is better when the order of arrival must be maintained. This is useful for managing tasks waiting in line, like at a bank.
asks: Can I use a queue for waiting tasks?

faq.q: How do I traverse a tree structure?
faq.a: Tree traversal means visiting every node in the tree exactly once. Common methods include in-order, pre-order, and post-order traversal.
asks: What are the types of tree traversal?
How do I visit all nodes in a tree?

faq.a: No, a tree does not have to be balanced. A balanced tree keeps the height difference between the left and right sides small for efficiency.

faq.q: What is the difference between enqueue and push?
faq.a: Push is used specifically for adding an item to the top of a stack. Enqueue is used for adding an item to the rear of a queue.
asks: Which operation adds to the end?
Can I use push for a queue?

facts: Stacks operate on the LIFO principle.
Queues operate on the FIFO principle.
Tree traversal systematically visits every node in the tree.
The root node is the topmost node in a tree structure.

quiz.say: If you push A, then B, then C onto a stack, what is the first item popped?
quiz.why: Because the last item pushed (C) is the first one to come out (LIFO).

wrong.0: This assumes the structure is First In First Out, which is incorrect for a stack.
wrong.1: This is incorrect because the rule dictates the most recently added item must leave first.
wrong.2: This suggests an order that does not follow the strict LIFO rule.

quiz.say: In a queue, if items X, Y, Z are enqueued in that order, which item is dequeued next?
quiz.why: Queues follow FIFO, meaning the first item in (X) is the first one out.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because the item that has been waiting the longest must be processed next.
wrong.1: Only one item can be dequeued at a time following the queue rules.
wrong.3: This violates the FIFO rule; the last item added cannot leave first.

quiz.say: Which traversal method processes the left child before the right child?
quiz.why: In-order traversal visits Left Subtree, then the Root, then the Right Subtree.

wrong.0: Traversal methods must follow a defined, predictable order.
wrong.2: Pre-order visits the Root first, before visiting the subtrees.
wrong.3: Post-order visits all children first, and only processes the Root last.
